input.reasoning_summary:
The claim makes two assertions about Adobe's fiscal 2025: (1) revenue grew in every region, and (2) cash generated from operations declined.

REVENUE BY REGION (SUPPORTED): Evidence E13 explicitly states "Overall revenue during fiscal 2025 increased in all geographic regions as compared to fiscal 2024" and provides the data showing all three regions (Americas, EMEA, APAC) experienced year-over-year growth: Americas grew 10%, EMEA grew 13%, and APAC grew 10%. This portion of the claim is fully supported.

OPERATING CASH FLOW (CONTRADICTED): The evidence clearly contradicts the claim that cash from operations declined. Evidence E19 shows that "Net cash provided by operating activities" was $10,031 million in fiscal 2025 compared to $8,056 million in fiscal 2024, representing an increase of approximately $1,975 million or 24.5% year-over-year growth. This is the opposite of a decline.

The challenges investigated whether: (H1) revenue actually grew in all regions - REFUTED, the evidence confirms it did grow in all regions; (H2) whether working capital or one-time items explain the discrepancy - no relevant evidence found to support this; (H3) whether different terminology might show a decline - REFUTED, the standard "net cash provided by operating activities" metric shows an increase, not a decline.

Since one material part of the claim (operating cash flow declined) is directly contradicted by the evidence, the overall claim is CONTRADICTED.

The evidence review confirms these passages are valid and directly address the claim's assertions - E13 ENTAILS the revenue portion, while E19/E10/E11 CONTRADICT the cash flow portion. Since the claim is materially false regarding operating cash flow, the verdict changes to CONTRADICTED.
